correctness.rationale: Under the frozen Finding's literal definition (for every selected s, S minus s is identifying), S=∅ qualifies vacuously. This contradicts the no-large-omissions assertion, the polynomial's zero constant term, and minimum size ten. In fact, with that literal condition ∅ is the only inclusion-minimal valid set. Step 1 omits this counterexample. The C++ checker explicitly filters out the zero mask via `if(ok && c)`; the Python checker also excludes it by its stronger two-selected-elements tests. For the standard convention requiring S itself to be an identifying code, the mathematics checks out: the only forbidden triples for omissions of size at most four occur in a closed neighborhood or in the four-element symmetric difference at an incidence. A pure triple is forbidden precisely by collinearity or concurrency; in a mixed triple two incidences violate domination, zero incidences violate the four-element symmetric-difference test at the intersection of the two lines and its join to the point, and one incidence passes both tests. This yields the cap and matching four-types and excludes mixed five-sets and pure five-caps. Independent script /workspace/review-evidence/heawood.py tested all 16,384 subsets directly by deleting one vertex and comparing traces, rejected the one vacuous candidate by requiring nonemptiness, matched every corrected feasible mask to the geometry and found the stated polynomial, 98 inclusion-minimal codes, and group/orbits 336 and 14+84. This validates the conventional version only; no corrected claim is submitted because substantive novelty does not survive.
residual_risks: The punctured definition may be read informally as presupposing an identifying code; even with that convention the originality failure is decisive.

evidence: The matched family of permitted four-omissions has a triple shadow consisting of noncollinear/nonconcurrent pure triples (56 total) and one-incidence mixed triples (168 total). A noncollinear triple of binary vectors x,y,z completes by x+y+z; a mixed triple completes by choosing a point on the unmatched line, off the other line, or dually. Conversely every such triple in a minimum omission has that geometry. This gives all 224 triples by the matched coefficient; smaller omissions are already all subsets by the matched binomial coefficients or by extending to these triples. This directly gives inclusion-minimality. The two minimum families are automatically transitive: linear maps act transitively on lines and duality joins both shores; for two induced matches x–ker f, y–ker g, choose z spanning ker f ∩ ker g. Then (x,y,z) is a basis in which both functionals have fixed coordinates, proving transitivity by change of basis. The connected bipartition makes pure and mixed types inequivalent.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The matched theorem does not expressly state the triple rule or both orbits, but supplies the complete four-family and the exact census, so the extra clauses are routine consequences, not a surviving substantial exact classification under another name.
